The picker applies rotational tension to the plug with a tension wrench. This tension compresses the springs of the unset pins, holding them in place.

As the rake continues to twist, it eventually sets a specific pin cluster at the shear line. Because the tension wrench holds the plug steady, this newly set pin cannot fall back down; instead, the rotational force transfers directly to the plug, causing it to rotate and open the lock. The physics relies on friction, spring compression, and the precise alignment of the shear line.
